name: Algum
overview: The Scripture references to Algum, also known as Almug or Almuggim trees, highlight their significance in the construction and ornamentation of the house of the LORD and the king's palace. These rare and precious trees, brought from Ophir and Lebanon by the navy of Hiram and Solomon's servants, were crafted into pillars, terraces, harps, and psalteries for singers, demonstrating their value and sacred use in worship and royal settings. The uniqueness of Algum wood, noted as unseen before or since in Judah, underscores its special role in the biblical narrative of temple building and worship.
